newsitem.title: USA: NFA disciplines firm for deceptive radio ads.
newsitem.headline: NFA disciplines firm for deceptive radio ads.

text.p: The National Futures Association (NFA) said it has expelled Commonwealth Financial Group Inc and barred the firm's president from associating with any NFA member.

The NFA said it found that Commonwealth and Charles Hoffecker, the firm's president and sole principal, had produced and aired misleading radio advertisements, failed to surpervise their employees and engaged in a deliberate course of conduct designed to defraud and deceive customers.
The NFA added that it also found the firm had engaged in fraudulent and misleading sales solicitations.

NFA, a congressionally authorized self-regulatory body for the futures industry, stated it fined Commonwealth $100,000 and Hoffecker $250,000. Commonwealth is an introducing broker based in Ft Lauderdale, Florida.
After five years, the firm may reapply for NFA membership and Hoffecker may apply to be associated with a NFA member, the NFA said.
Seven futures brokers at Commonwealth were also found to have engaged in fraudulent and deceptive sales solicitations, the NFA added.
The NFA said it imposed fines of $2,000 to $15,000 and restrictions on six of the brokers, of which four were barred from association with any NFA member for six months.
One of the seven brokers was permanently barred from association with any NFA member after he failed to file a response to the NFA complaint, it added.
